note: Who the portal says an account is, and the pair the client's login message will carry. This is this project's own and it is temporary: a real identity store is a schema decision and the login database has no account table yet. A name not listed answers the reference's own refusal: 400 who are you?

information.what: A record list, not a set of settings: each row is one account a client may log in as.
information.what the pair is: user_id is the portal's own identifier and token is what the login message carries; the client sends both back verbatim, so they are what an identity check will compare against.
information.why it exists: docs/decisions/0003-portal-host.md - the portal is served by the auth program, and this file is who it answers for.
information.to remove: When the identity question is decided, these rows become a table and this file becomes a seed for it.

accounts.doc: The name this machine's client types, with the password 123. It is first because a client asked to log in as it and the server refused while the name was absent.
A second name, so that a test can log in as somebody and still be somebody else.
